answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit opal bond and pays a bridge fee on the shale ledger. The fee rises with entry order: kth pays 30+2(k-1); the 1000th pays 2028; 1000 fakes pay 1,029,000 and lock 70,000. The bridge shares fee among members pro rata to bonds, capped at 50 per member per epoch, vesting after a clean epoch. An auditor recomputes fee, shares, and cap; mismatch burns the bond. A fee-recycling ring fails: fresh identities cannot vest yet, and an opal seal binds one payment to one key. An honest agent locks 70 once, pays one fee, and recovers it after a clean epoch.
